findings.title: Published install instructions install an unrelated PyPI project instead of Opaque
findings.claim: The repository is public and its documentation site is live. The 'From JetBrains Packages' commands correctly pass --index-url (installation.md:20, :27; README.md:68, :72), but the 'Extras' block immediately below them drops it: `pip install "opaque[auditing]"`, `"opaque[dpftrl]"`, `"opaque[transformers]"`, `"opaque[all]"`. With no index override pip resolves `opaque` from PyPI, where that name belongs to a different project entirely - `opaque` 1.0.0, 'python libopaque wrapper' by Stefan Marsiske (https://github.com/stef/libopaque). The extras are silently ignored (pip only warns about unknown extras), so the user ends up with an unrelated cryptography binding and no Opaque at all. The Opaque distribution names are largely unclaimed on PyPI: `opaque-dpsgd` 404s, and `opaque-accounting` resolves to a metadata-less 999.9.9 placeholder, so the namespace is not defensively held.
findings.failure_scenario: A reader of https://jetbrains-research.github.io/opaque/latest/getting-started/installation/ (live, verified 200) wants DP-FTRL. They copy `pip install "opaque[dpftrl]"` from the Extras block. pip downloads opaque-1.0.0.tar.gz from PyPI and installs a libopaque wrapper; `import opaque.dpftrl` then fails with ModuleNotFoundError and the user concludes the library is broken. Reproduced verbatim in a clean venv: `pip install --dry-run --no-deps "opaque[auditing]"` prints 'Downloading opaque-1.0.0.tar.gz (10 kB)' and 'Would install opaque-1.0.0'. Because `opaque-dpsgd` is an unclaimed name on PyPI, the same missing-index pattern is also the shape a dependency-confusion upload would exploit.

findings.line: code cell 13 (theoretical bound); training loop in code cell 9
findings.claim: This is the exact OPQ-355 defect, alive in a sibling notebook that #843's fix did not touch and that the new CI step does not execute. Cell 9 trains with `DataLoader(train_data, batch_size=batch_size, shuffle=True)` - fixed-size shuffled batches, not Poisson sampling. Cell 13 then computes `process = dpsgd_acc.poisson(dpsgd_acc.gaussian(noise_multiplier), sample_rate) * total_steps` and prints it as 'Theoretical epsilon'. Poisson subsampling amplification does not hold for shuffled fixed-size batches; the conservative analysis for that loop is unamplified composition. The notebook then compares the audited epsilon against this understated ceiling and prints 'OK: audited epsilon is within the theoretical bound', which is precisely the sanity check .junie/differential-privacy-review.md says must be sound ('treat an empirical lower bound above the theoretical upper bound as a likely defect'). Cell 9 additionally divides the noised sum by the realised batch size (`p - (lr / bs) * g`) rather than a fixed expected batch size, so the released update is a function of a data-dependent quantity the mechanism never noised - the fixed dp_sgd_training.ipynb explicitly comments the opposite ('Gradients are already normalized by the fixed expected batch size').
findings.failure_scenario: With the notebook's own parameters (noise_multiplier=0.5, batch_size=64, n_epochs=200, ~250 training examples after the coin flip, so total_steps=600 and sample_rate=0.256) the published 'Theoretical epsilon' is 253.2 while the conservative no-amplification bound for the same 600 releases is 1408.9 - a 5.6x understatement. A reader who copies this pattern (shuffled DataLoader + Poisson-amplified accountant) into their own run reports an epsilon 5.6x smaller than anything they can justify, and the notebook's audit 'OK' line actively confirms the wrong number. The same notebook is what the auditing guide points readers at.
evidence: docs/tutorials/privacy_auditing.ipynb code cell 9: `train_loader = DataLoader(train_data, batch_size=batch_size, shuffle=True)` then `params = tuple(p - (lr / bs) * g for p, g in zip(params, noisy_grads.pytree))`

docs/tutorials/privacy_auditing.ipynb code cell 13: `sample_rate = batch_size / len(train_data)`; `total_steps = n_epochs * (len(train_data) // batch_size)`; `process = dpsgd_acc.poisson(dpsgd_acc.gaussian(noise_multiplier), sample_rate) * total_steps`; `theoretical_eps = process.epsilon_at(1e-5)`; `if audited_eps <= theoretical_eps: print("OK: ...")`
docs/tutorials/privacy_auditing.ipynb code cell 7: noise_multiplier = 0.5, batch_size = 64, n_epochs = 200; cell 3: n_samples = 500; cell 5: coin_flip over all 500 leaves ~250 in-canaries
Computed with the shipped accountant at n_train=250: poisson-amplified eps = 253.222, unamplified (dpsgd_acc.gaussian(0.5) * 600) eps = 1408.936, ratio 5.6x

findings.title: Sweep A's executable-docs gate executes no Markdown snippet and only 3 of 7 notebooks
findings.claim: Issue #843's acceptance criteria were 'Every documented accounting and training snippet executes as written, in CI' and 'The executable-docs check runs on every PR, so this class cannot recur silently'. The step 12146ec4 added executes exactly three things: `examples/quickstart.py`, `python -m doctest packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/accounting/__init__.py`, and three of the seven tutorial notebooks. It executes zero of the 369 ```python fences spread across 46 Markdown files under docs/ - including every snippet the ten Sweep A findings were about. The one page that is genuinely protected (quickstart.md) is protected because it was rewritten to transclude the executed script, which is the right pattern but was applied to exactly one page. Nothing prevents the next accounting snippet from drifting, which is the recurrence the issue set out to stop. The same gap exists on main: docs.yml deploys the public site on every push with `mike deploy` (a non-strict mkdocs build) and no doc-execution step at all, so the strict build and the execution step exist only on the PR path.
findings.failure_scenario: A future PR changes an accounting factory signature and updates the reference table but not the snippet in docs/user-guide/accounting.md. `mkdocs build --strict` still passes (it does not execute code), the three notebooks and quickstart.py still pass (they do not use that snippet), and the drifted snippet ships to the public docs site. This is the same mechanism that produced OPQ-357, OPQ-361, OPQ-362, OPQ-363, OPQ-364 and OPQ-365 in the first place. The residual `optimizer.step()` call in reference/rng.md (filed separately) is a live instance that survived Sweep A itself.

findings.title: Per-group Gaussian noise has no realized-vs-reported conformance test; a 3% shortfall passes the whole suite
findings.claim: OPQ-378's fix sketch named three shapes: 'gaussian_noise, per-group gaussian_noise and mf_gaussian_noise'. PR #871 delivered scalar gaussian_noise and six mf_gaussian_noise strategies but not the per-group path, and no other test binds realized per-group noise magnitude to the reported PerGroup noise_stddev. The only magnitude assertion for per-group noise is a ratio check on 100 samples (`mlp_var > attn_var * 2.5`), which is invariant to a uniform scale error, and test_gaussian_second_moment.py / test_paired_noise_stddevs.py only assert that the reported metadata is a PerGroup of the right values. The paired second-moment streams have the same gap.
findings.failure_scenario: Verified by targeted mutation. With a plugin that makes only the per-group lookup inside gaussian_noise's `_add_noise_tree` return 0.97x its value - so the drawn noise is 3% low while `output.noise_stddev` still reports the correct PerGroup and the accountant is still charged `gaussian(nm)` - the entire PR-gate suite for opaque-dpsgd plus opaque-engine passes: 1355 passed, 26 skipped, 148 deselected, 0 failed. The same 3% shortfall applied globally (scaling torch.randn) is caught by 10 tests. So a regression in the per-group cast/lookup path - an fp32/bf16 round trip, a wrong ParamPath resolution, a recomputed group bound - ships green while users at a reported nm are charged for noise they did not receive.

packages/opaque-dpsgd/tests/noise/test_noise.py:129-139 and packages/opaque-dpftrl/tests/noise/test_realized_stddev.py:41-48,101-158 - the seven new conformance tests, all scalar-stddev

Mutation A (global, torch.randn * 0.97) over packages/opaque-dpsgd/tests/noise + packages/opaque-dpftrl/tests/noise: 10 failed, 372 passed (baseline 382 passed) - failures include all 7 conformance cases
Mutation B (PerGroup.for_path * 0.97 only when the caller frame is `_add_noise_tree`) over packages/opaque-dpsgd + packages/opaque-engine under the PR marker: 1355 passed, 26 skipped, 0 failed

findings.fix_sketch: Add two cases to the existing `_assert_realized_stddev_matches_reported` helper: one `gaussian_noise` call with a PerGroup max_norm over two 5e5-element leaves, asserting each leaf's realized RMS against `output.noise_stddev.for_path(path)` at 6/sqrt(2n); and one paired `SecondMomentClippingOutput` case checking both `noisy_grads` and `noisy_squared_grads` against their respective reported stddevs. Both are cheap and belong in the same file as the scalar case.

findings.title: TRY003 was enabled in the same commit that introduced a 179-site idiom Ruff cannot see, so the new lint rule enforces nothing
findings.claim: 7b26f655 (PR #760, 'feat(exceptions): add public exception taxonomy') moved TRY003 from `ignore` into `select` and, in the same commit, rewrote 158 raise sites into the form `raise SomeError(*("message",))`. Ruff's TRY003 matches a long message passed as a positional argument to the exception constructor; a starred tuple is not matched, so every one of those sites is invisible to the rule. The count is now 179 across packages/*/src and was 0 at 4b13d82. The same commit also added TRY003 to the per-file-ignores for `**/tests/**` and `tests/**`, so the rule is disabled in every test tree as well. The result is a lint rule that is nominally part of the merge gate and cannot fire. The comment block that documents the choice still lists TRY003 under 'Omitted only when they fight intentional design', contradicting the `select` entry three lines below it. ff174f11 (PR #897), whose subject is 'restore the lint gate by fixing three TRY003 violations', converted its three findings into exactly this splat form rather than into message-carrying exception classes.
findings.failure_scenario: A contributor writes `raise ConfigurationError(f"bands must be >= 1, got {bands}")` the obvious way. Ruff flags TRY003 and the autoformat gate fails. The contributor greps the codebase, finds 179 examples of `raise ConfigurationError(*("...",))`, copies that, and the gate goes green - having changed nothing about the property the rule exists to enforce, while making the call site harder to read and defeating any type checker's arity check on the constructor. Meanwhile the repository carries a merge-gate rule whose violation count is structurally pinned at zero. Verified: `ruff check --select TRY003 packages/ tests/` -> 'All checks passed!'.
evidence: pyproject.toml:248 - "TRY003" in [tool.ruff.lint].select; pyproject.toml:261-267 - `ignore` no longer contains it

pyproject.toml:215-223 - the 'Omitted only when they fight intentional design' comment block still lists TRY003 with the rationale 'public semantic categories carry stable catch contracts without a bespoke exception class per diagnostic message'
pyproject.toml:299-300 - `"**/tests/**" = ["INP001", "D", "PLR2004", "TRY003"]` and the same for `"tests/**"`
git grep -E 'raise [A-Za-z_]+(Error|Exception)\(\*\(' -- packages : 0 hits at 4b13d82, 179 hits at 12146ec4
git show 7b26f655 -- pyproject.toml shows the select/per-file-ignores change; the same commit adds 158 `(*(` raise sites across 170 files
git show ff174f11 converts `raise ValueError("dataset_size must be provided ...")` into `raise ConfigurationError(*("dataset_size must be provided ...",))`

Reproduced: `raise E(f"n_steps must be >= 1, got {n}")` piped through `ruff check --select TRY003 --stdin-filename packages/opaque-engine/src/.../probe.py -` -> TRY003, exit 1; the identical code as `raise E(*(f"...",))` -> 'All checks passed!', exit 0
`ruff check --no-cache --select TRY003 packages/ tests/` on the current tree -> 'All checks passed!'
findings.fix_sketch: Decide which it is and make the config say so. Either keep TRY003 in `ignore` with the existing rationale and revert the 179 splats to plain string arguments (they read better and type-check), or keep the rule and give the exception taxonomy message-carrying constructors so the splat is unnecessary. Either way, fix the comment at pyproject.toml:215-223 so it no longer documents TRY003 as omitted while selecting it.

findings.title: The per-package wheel build inventory in build-distributions.yml has no coverage guard
findings.claim: OPQ-380 named two hand-maintained inventories: the test-package matrix in python-tests.yml and the per-package build steps in build-distributions.yml. PR #870 guarded the first and left the second untouched. build-distributions.yml still has ten literal `uv build packages/opaque-<name> --wheel --out-dir dist` steps (plus opaque-accounting in the separate native job) and nothing checks that list against `packages/*`. This is the higher-stakes of the two inventories: a package missing from the test matrix runs no tests, while a package missing here is never built and never published. The downstream checks do not close it either - `validate-distributions.yml:68` asserts only `len(opaque_versions) > 1`, and `check_wheel_internal_pins.py` validates pins on the wheels that exist rather than checking that all expected wheels do.
findings.failure_scenario: A contributor adds `packages/opaque-<new>/` with a tests/ tree and a pyproject. The new #870 guard correctly fails the lane until they add it to python-tests.yml, so the tests get wired up. Nothing forces the corresponding edit to build-distributions.yml. If the umbrella `opaque` distribution does not depend on the new package (the common case for an optional stack), no wheel is ever built, `validate-distributions` still passes (`len(opaque_versions) > 1` holds), and both the dev-wheel publish on main and the release publish ship a set that silently omits it. Users installing from the JetBrains index get an ImportError for a package the repository documents.
evidence: .github/workflows/build-distributions.yml:46-74 - ten hardcoded 'Build opaque-*' steps; opaque-accounting is built separately at :141-163
.github/workflows/python-tests.yml:102-125 - the guard added by 6de5f9ca, scoped to the suite matrix only, reading its own file
.github/workflows/validate-distributions.yml:61-69 - `assert len(opaque_versions) > 1` is the only completeness check on the published set
.github/scripts/check_wheel_internal_pins.py:188-195 - iterates `args.wheel_dir.glob("*.whl")`, i.e. only the wheels that were built
OPQ-380 evidence line: '`build-distributions.yml:73-74` hardcodes per-package build steps the same way'
findings.fix_sketch: Either replace the ten steps with a loop over `packages/*/pyproject.toml` (excluding opaque-accounting, which maturin builds), or add the same comm-based guard used in python-tests.yml as a first step of build-python-wheels. A stronger alternative: have check_wheel_internal_pins.py additionally assert that the set of dist names found in --wheel-dir equals the set of `project.name` values across the root and packages/*/pyproject.toml.

findings.title: The value-level CachedProcess.repeated_pld regression test was deleted one day after it landed, leaving only a mock with no real implementor
findings.claim: OPQ-379 asked for a value-level epsilon assertion on a correlated strategy because the surviving guards used the one strategy where the buggy and correct answers coincide. PR #885 added exactly that (`test_cached_correlated_full_horizon_preserves_epsilon`, band_mf bands=16, n_steps=128) on 2026-09-02. 87404a1b (PR #894) deleted packages/opaque-dpftrl/tests/accounting/test_per_step.py in full on 2026-09-03, taking that test with the acc.per_step API it depended on. What remains is the mock test in test_cached.py, which patches `repeated_pld` onto an `eps_delta` process to manufacture a divergence. After #894 there is no subclass in the tree that overrides `repeated_pld` other than CachedProcess itself, so the relay is a no-op on every shipped process and the mock is guarding a contract nothing currently implements - while `DpProcess.repeated_pld`'s own docstring still invites subclasses to override it.
findings.failure_scenario: Verified by mutation: `del CachedProcess.repeated_pld` over packages/opaque-accounting/tests + packages/opaque-dpftrl/tests/accounting + packages/opaque-dpsgd/tests/accounting gives 1 failed / 601 passed, and the single failure is the mock test. The exposure is forward-looking: when a future mechanism reintroduces a count-sensitive `repeated_pld` override (the docstring at _base.py:428-433 explicitly anticipates 'DP-FTRL per-step adapters, where K steps' joint PLD depends on the deployed N-step strategy's correlation matrix'), the only thing standing between that and a silent reversion to `pld().self_compose(K)` is a mock that will still pass because it patches its own stub. OPQ-005 measured that divergence at 2.17x epsilon for band_mf(bands=16), n=128, K=128.

Mutation `del CachedProcess.repeated_pld` over the three accounting test trees under the PR marker: 1 failed, 601 passed; the failure is test_cached.py::test_cached_process_preserves_repeated_pld_override with 'assert 3.0 == 2.0'
packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/api/accounting/core/_base.py:428-433 - docstring still says subclasses whose K-fold behaviour differs 'override this to compute the true K-step PLD directly'
findings.fix_sketch: Keep the mock test, and add a real one next to it: define a two-line DpProcess subclass in the test file whose `repeated_pld(count)` returns a demonstrably different PLD from `pld().self_compose(count)`, wrap it in `acc.cached(...)`, and assert `(cached * n).epsilon_at(delta) == (inner * n).epsilon_at(delta)` while `inner.pld().self_compose(n).epsilon_at(delta)` differs. That guards the relay against both deletion and a wrong-count relay without depending on any mechanism that may later be removed.

findings.title: Python 3.12 is claimed by eleven pyproject classifiers with zero CI coverage and no documented endpoints-only policy
findings.claim: Issue #841 (OPQ-386) was closed as not_planned. Neither of its two acceptance branches was taken: there is still no 3.12 leg anywhere, and the endpoints-only choice is not written down as a policy in AGENTS.md or CONTRIBUTING.md, both of which enumerate the lanes in detail. `grep -rn '3\.12' .github/` returns zero hits across all fourteen workflows, four composite actions and nine scripts, while `requires-python = ">=3.11,<3.14"` resolves 3.12 and every distribution ships the 3.12 classifier. The second-order cost is that the next reader of the lane list cannot tell whether 3.12 is untested by decision or by the accident of the #665 version bump that retargeted the 3.12 lanes to 3.13.

findings.title: docs/reference/rng.md calls optimizer.step(), which the functional optimizer does not have
findings.claim: reference/rng.md was one of the pages Sweep A (#843) covered - OPQ-362 was specifically about this file, and 12146ec4 changed 22 lines in it, correcting every gaussian_noise call to keyword form. The determinism example a few lines above those fixes still ends with `optimizer.step(noisy_grads)`. `opaque.optimizers.sgd(...)` returns a `torchopt.base.GradientTransformation` whose public members are `chain, count, index, init, update`; there is no `step`. Every other end-to-end snippet in the docs uses the correct `updates, opt_state = optimizer.update(...)` then `torchopt.apply_updates(...)` pair. This is a concrete instance of the gap in the previous finding: the page was hand-edited and the wrong line survived because nothing executes it.
findings.failure_scenario: A reader following the RNG reference to wire per-step keys into a training loop copies the block and gets `AttributeError: 'GradientTransformation' object has no attribute 'step'` at the first step. The surrounding lines are correct, so the natural conclusion is that the optimizer import is wrong rather than the doc. The same block also calls an undefined `compute_dp_grads(model, batch)`, so it cannot run as written in any case.
evidence: docs/reference/rng.md:305-325 - the fenced example ending `noisy_grads, state = noise_fn(grads, state)` then `optimizer.step(noisy_grads)`
`from opaque.optimizers import sgd; o = sgd(lr=0.01)` -> `<class 'torchopt.base.GradientTransformation'>`, public members ['chain', 'count', 'index', 'init', 'update'], `hasattr(o, 'step')` is False
grep -rn 'optimizer\.step' docs/ examples/ -> exactly one hit, docs/reference/rng.md:325
Contrast docs/user-guide/dp-sgd.md:148-149 and examples/quickstart.py:88-89, which both use `updates, opt_state = optimizer.update(...)` + `torchopt.apply_updates(params, updates)`
git show 12146ec4 -- docs/reference/rng.md - 22 lines changed in this file by the Sweep A commit, none of them line 325
findings.fix_sketch: Replace line 325 with the standard pair (`updates, opt_state = optimizer.update(noisy_grads, opt_state); params = torchopt.apply_updates(params, updates)`) and either define or drop the `compute_dp_grads` placeholder so the block is runnable, then bring the page under whatever snippet-execution mechanism closes the previous finding.

findings.title: Sweep B's structural criterion is unmet: no generator or CI check ties published defaults and accepted-value lists to their dataclasses
findings.claim: Issue #844 opened by observing that '#419 reconciled the tables once by hand; they drifted again, so the fix needs to be a generator or a check rather than another pass', and its first acceptance criterion was 'Every published default and accepted-value list is generated from, or checked against, its dataclass in CI'. PR #1026 performed another hand pass. The tables are correct today - I checked the mechanism/sampler/default-kwargs table line by line against _training_arguments.py:189-262 and the delta default at :265-270 - but no generator and no check exists, so the same drift mechanism that produced OPQ-358, OPQ-360 and OPQ-369 is untouched.
findings.failure_scenario: The next change to `_MECHANISM_DEFAULT_KWARGS` or `_ALLOWED_SAMPLING_MODES` - for instance the follow-up to #1010 that already changed mf_band's default sampler to cyclic_poisson - updates the dataclass and forgets the table. Nothing in CI notices; `mkdocs build --strict` does not read Python, and the only tests that mention a docs path are two unrelated prose comments. A user then configures `sampling_mode` from a stale accepted-value list and gets a construction error, or copies a stale default and silently trains a different mechanism than the docs describe. OPQ-369's half of this family was epsilon-affecting (a documented target delta that did not match the computed one).
evidence: docs/user-guide/huggingface/training-arguments.md:148-155 - the hand-written mechanism/sampler/default-kwargs table; :159-165 the prose accepted-value list

packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_training_arguments.py:189-210 (_MECHANISM_SAMPLERS, allowed sampling modes) and :254-262 (default kwargs) - the source of truth the table duplicates

grep -rln 'docs/' over packages/*/tests and tests/ -> packages/opaque-patches/tests/torch/test_cpu_offload.py:106 and tests/integration/alignment/test_mechanism_agnostic.py:3, both prose comments; no test reads a docs file
git show ba39783d (PR #1026, closing #844) - a documentation-only edit; no generator, no test, no CI step added
docs/reference/transformers.md:188,192 - a second hand-maintained copy of the same defaults, which must now be kept in sync with both the dataclass and training-arguments.md
findings.fix_sketch: Add one package-local test in packages/opaque-transformers/tests that imports `_MECHANISM_SAMPLERS`, `_ALLOWED_SAMPLING_MODES`, `_MECHANISM_DEFAULT_KWARGS` and `_DEFAULT_PRIVACY_DELTA_EXPONENT`, parses the Markdown table out of docs/user-guide/huggingface/training-arguments.md, and asserts equality both ways (no documented mechanism missing, no undocumented mechanism present, kwargs dicts identical). That is a structural check on machine-readable content, not prose pinning, so it is consistent with the repository's test-design rule. Alternatively generate the table into a partial and transclude it with pymdownx.snippets, the way quickstart.md now transcludes its script.
